staging.environment: Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64, Linux 6.8.0-147-generic, QEMU with no network device; only guest loopback was up
staging.transport: Real TCP connections to the PathWard HTTP listener and two independent loopback application listeners. Each application recorded POST bodies in its own file and called sync_data before responding or disconnecting.

tests.name: refused_before_send_switches_and_records_one_write
tests.fault: A closes its listening socket before returning 204 to the outstanding health check. Its subsequent application connect is refused.

tests.name: lost_response_after_durable_write_does_not_replay
tests.fault: A commits the POST and closes its connection before sending any response headers.

tests.name: drain_preserves_dispatched_work_and_excludes_new_writes
tests.observed: A held its first response during reload and completed it. A previously captured generation refused a new dispatch. B handled the second POST. Draining both returned 503. Reactivating A allowed the fourth POST.

tests.name: longest_route_owns_its_members_and_an_empty_pool_never_falls_through
tests.observed: Healthy members alternated on the parent route. The nested route selected its own member. After draining it, the nested POST returned 503 and all three ledgers were empty.

tests.name: unhealthy_members_are_skipped_and_recover_while_idle
tests.observed: With both health endpoints returning 503 the POST was refused. B recovered on a background probe with no new frontend traffic. The next POST was recorded only on B.

publication_staging.entry_points: Unprivileged pathward-hosting build read the root-owned fixture policy and used the real pathward-server check. The generated KDL contained the complete route membership, health path and drain. A second direct pathward-server check accepted that candidate.

proofs.scope: The extracted Rust selector returns only a ready, undrained member of the supplied route before dispatch. The first dispatch consumes a per-request grant. Later selection and dispatch cannot grant another write for that request.
proofs.open: Runtime lock, health, and socket correspondence is tracked as LOCAL-POOL-ADAPTER-REFINEMENT in proofs/roadmap.json. Independently retried requests require an application operation ID and deduplication.
